# UNDERWRITING MEMORANDUM — LAMAR ADVERTISING COMPANY (LAMR)

---

## SECTION 0 — OVERVIEW

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Ticker / Company | LAMR — Lamar Advertising Company (REIT-Specialty, outdoor advertising) |
| Price T0 (2026-10-05) | $143.93 [Actual] |
| Market cap | $14.76B [Actual] |
| **Verdict** | **HOLD on value; Accumulate (momentum basis, smaller size)** |
| Base IV | $137.38 (−4.6% vs price) |
| Bull IV | $154.30 (+7.2%) |
| Bear IV | $87.81 (−39.0%) |
| Probability-weighted IV | $129.22 → expected return **−10.2%** |
| Margin of safety at T0 | **None on value** (price sits 4.8% above Base; payoff skew 0.18x) |

The price is paying roughly what the business is worth — slightly more, once the Bear case is weighted in. Value alone says stand aside. But the uptrend is strong and is backed by the company's own filings (raised guidance, record margin, raised dividend), so a trend-disciplined, smaller momentum position is justified under mandate 7. The honest value direction stays HOLD; I do not raise the value to flatter the trend.

---

## SECTION 1 — MACRO (DATA 1.5 / 1.6)

- **Rates:** 10y nominal 5.28%, real 2.92%, breakeven 2.36%; curve +0.47% (steepening). COE ANCHOR **8.62%**; terminal-growth default **3.75%** [Actual, pack anchors]. A 5.3% 10y is the binding constraint on REIT-style multiples — LAMR trades ~26x trailing GAAP P/E while the real-estate sector band median is 23.2x (p25 10.5x) [DATA 8.5].
- **Regime vector (2026-10-01):** goldilocks 0.341 / reflation 0.271 / tightening 0.176 / stagflation 0.130 / recession 0.081 — headline goldilocks, contested (margin 0.070). The 21% combined recession+stagflation tail is the demand risk to outdoor ad budgets; the 17.6% tightening probability is the multiple-compression risk.
- **Active shock:** `oil_shock` severity 1, direction up (onset 2026-09-28) — energy price spike from Hormuz disruption. LAMR exposure is second-order: fuel/production costs are a small slice of billboard opex; the real channel is inflation stickiness (CPI 3.35%, PCE 3.42%) keeping rates elevated, which compresses rate-sensitive REIT valuations and pressures advertiser budgets.
- **Credit:** IG spread 1.47%, HY OAS 3.10% — refinancing of LAMR's ~$3.5B debt stack remains orderly; no credit-tightening trigger visible in the pack.

**Net:** macro is a headwind to the multiple, neutral-to-supportive to the cash flow (ad budgets resilient, political cycle peaking in H2 2026). This asymmetry — cash flow holding up while the multiple is rate-capped — is exactly why value and momentum diverge here.

---

## SECTION 2 — BUSINESS & MOAT

### Economic engines (mandate 1)

**a) Transactional deliveries — billboard advertising (the core, cyclical).** Billboard = $2,013.9M of $2,266.2M FY2025 revenue (88.9%) [Actual, PRIMARY P3]. Q2 2026: revenue +6.5% reported / +6.1% acquisition-adjusted; direct advertising expense is ~31.6% of revenue ($194.7M/$616.7M H1 2026) [Actual, PRIMARY P1] — meaning roughly two-thirds of the P&L below the ad-cost line is semi-fixed (G&A $90.8M + corporate $27.9M per quarter), so revenue shocks deleverage ~2:1 into EBITDA. Digital conversion capex is the growth lever: $34.7M digital capex in H1 2026 [Actual, PRIMARY P1].

**b) Captive installed base / recurring annuity.** 360,000+ displays on long-term easements across the US and Canada; largest US digital network (5,700+ displays) [Actual, PRIMARY P4]. Logo signs (interstate/local business signage) and transit/airport are quasi-annuity: local/regional advertisers renew continuously — 17 straight quarters of local/regional strength per the catalyst brief [Unconfirmed, third-party]. **However:** the filings in the pack contain no quantified multi-year contracted backlog or % recurring revenue (DATA 12 confirms segment detail is not mapped). Per mandate 2 I credit **no** uncontracted annuity beyond what owner earnings already reflect — the easement land positions are the moat, not a booked contract stream.

**c) Strategic optionality.** Programmatic sales grew >50% in Q2 2026 and are ~10% of digital billboard revenue; national/programmatic revenue +16% [Estimate — company's own earnings call, reported by MarketBeat/investing.com 2026-08-07; transcript not in pack]. Digital revenue +15.4%, one-third of billboard revenue [same source]. This mix shift is what lifted adjusted EBITDA margin to a record 49.2% (+110 bps) [Actual, PRIMARY P1]. Management expects >$200M acquisition/easement spend in 2026 [Unconfirmed, secondary call summary].

### Owner earnings after SBC (mandate 2)
TTM owner earnings **$0.692B** (DATA 3: TTM NI $0.556B + π 99% × (D&A $0.326B − capex $0.189B)); SBC is already expensed in GAAP net income and is counted once via `sbc_treatment = deducted_in_cf` (FY2025 SBC $34M [Actual, DATA 5]). FY2026 company guidance implies owner earnings of ~$0.75–0.76B (guided NI $604.4–609.4M + total D&A ~$331M − capex ~$185–190M) [Estimate, arithmetic on PRIMARY P1].

### Moat rating (7 factors, 0–3 each → /21 → 1.0–5.0)

| Factor | Score | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Regulatory/permitting barriers | 3 | Zoning, easements and highway-corridor control gate new entrants; local opposition (Fairmont, WV [Unconfirmed, single case]) is friction on expansion, not a threat to the core |
| Scale & location scarcity | 3 | Largest US OOH operator by far; prime-exit land positions are irreplaceable [Actual, PRIMARY P4] |
| Switching costs | 1 | Advertisers shift budgets across OOH and digital channels; no quantified long-term contracts in filings |
| Network/data effects | 2 | 5,700+ digital screens + programmatic targeting is a real but young data moat |
| Cost advantage | 2 | Scale in production and easement economics; record 49.2% EBITDA margin vs peers |
| Brand/franchise | 2 | National brand advertisers; "most valuable OOH company in the world" is a CEO claim [Unconfirmed] |
| Lease/easement durability | 3 | Long-term easements; installed base compounds via M&A + digital conversion |

**Total 16/21 → moat 4.0 / 5.0, direction: expanding** (digital/programmatic mix shift is actively lifting margin [Actual]).

### Financial strength
Net debt $3.104B on FY2025 filed figures (LT $3.169B + current $0.250B − cash $0.065B) [Arithmetic, DATA 6]; the Q2 release shows total debt $3,514.5M at 2026-06-30 [Actual, PRIMARY P1] — consistent with the pack; the vendor's $4.919B appears to add operating leases ($1.487B) and is not used. H1 2026 interest expense $81.6M [Actual, PRIMARY P1]. Leverage ~2.9x per the brief [Estimate]. Dividend ≥$6.50/share in 2026 (≈$660M) vs guided FFO $885.6–890.6M → ~74% of FFO / ~73% of AFFO midpoint — affordable at 2.9x leverage but leaves little headroom if AFFO misses. Retained earnings negative (−$1.106B) is a REIT distribution artifact, not distress [Actual, DATA 6B].

---

## SECTION 3 — VALUATION

**Frame:** equity (all pack flows are after-interest). **Shares:** 101,549,684 (desk default). **Excess cash:** $0 (default; only $65M cash on file, de minimis). **Life:** perpetual — easement-based display fleet is not a depleting stock; the ~$76M/H1 replacement-and-conversion capex is already deducted in the base [Assumption, grounded in PRIMARY P1/P4].

| Input | Value | vs DEFAULT | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| base_cf | $0.692B | = default (TTM owner earnings) | none needed |
| Base growth yrs 1–5 | +9.8% / +6.6% / +3.9% / +3.9% / +3.9% | Yrs 1–2 deviate from desk-held levels ($0.873B/$0.934B) | **guidance_deviation_reason:** company's own FY2026 guidance (8-K filed 2026-08-06: NI $604.4–609.4M, RE D&A $310M guided) implies owner earnings of ~$0.75–0.76B, i.e. +8–10% on the TTM base — not the consensus-EPS-growth path ($+19.4%$ from the higher FY2025 reference base of $0.731B that embeds the $75.9M FY2025 asset-sale gain [Actual, DATA 5/P3]). Yrs 3–5 held at next-FY consensus revenue growth +3.9% (default). |
| fade_years | 5 | = default | reinvestment runway (digital conversion + M&A) justifies a 5-year glide to terminal |
| terminal_g | 3.75% | = default | between breakeven inflation 2.36% and the 3.75% anchor; own revenue trend 4.82%/yr supports it |
| terminal_ronic | 52.94% | = default | 8-year median return on tangible invested capital (2018–2025); billboard land earns structurally huge returns on book — the record's own evidence, no cap imposed |
| CoE (Base/Bull) | 8.62% | = COE ANCHOR | none needed |
| CoE (Bear) | 10.12% | +150 bps | mandate-4 cost-of-capital shock (tightening regime prob 17.6%, 10y at 5.28%) |
| Bear growth yrs 1–5 | +4.3% / −5.6% / +2.0% / +2.5% / +3.0% | — | post-midterm political normalization + ad-budget shock; see Section 4 |
| Bull growth yrs 1–5 | +14.0% / +10.1% / +6.5% / +5.5% / +4.5% | — | programmatic >50% persistence, digital mix, political upside; see Section 4 |

**Desk terminal (Base):** Gordon growth @ 3.8% on funded earnings, ROIC 52.9%; implied terminal EV/FCF multiple **21.3x**, terminal value = 58.3% of Base value. Gap to bands: 21.3x is *below* LAMR's current ~26.3x trailing GAAP P/E [Estimate, price/TTM EPS] and below the sector median trailing P/E of 23.2x / cluster peer median 22.6x [DATA 8.5] — defensible because the desk fades the operating margin from 37.6% (year 5) to 30.6% (year 10), i.e. it does not credit the record 49.2% EBITDA margin forever. Bear terminal multiple: 16.3x.

**Reverse DCF (mandate 3b):** under my structure, today's price implies **+6.16%** stage-1 (next-5y) cash-flow growth; under the neutral reference (8.62% CoE, 10y fade to 3.75%) it implies a **10-year CAGR of +3.65% — below the p50 base rate (5.6%)** for the $1–10B bucket [DATA 8 base rates]. The market is *not* pricing heroics: it prices ~consensus growth with a small premium in years 3–5 (price-implied +5.1% vs my +3.9%) and a slightly lower CoE (implied 8.38% vs 8.62%). My Base differs from the price only by ~5% — mainly because I anchor years 1–2 to company-guided owner earnings rather than consensus EPS growth, and hold years 3–5 at the single-analyst next-FY revenue estimate (+3.9%, n=1 [DATA 8] — a weak anchor I carry as uncertainty, not conviction).

**Crux:** none stated. The price is within ~5% of Base value and below Bull; there is no input on which my evidence says the market is materially wrong. Verdict per TASK item 6: **HOLD**.

## SECTION 4 — SCENARIOS (last complete desk run)

- **Bear — causal path:** 2026 is a midterm year: management says political revenue is >$5M ahead of last year and "tracking ahead of the 2024 election cycle" [Estimate, Q2 call via MarketBeat 2026-08-07], and AdImpact forecasts a record ~$11.6B cycle [Estimate, secondary, 2026-09-28]. H2 2026 is therefore loaded with one-time demand that mean-reverts in FY2027 (consensus already fades to +3.9% revenue). Layer on programmatic decelerating off a >50% base and a 10–15% ad-budget softening under sticky inflation (recession+stagflation regime prob 21%): with ~two-thirds of the cost base semi-fixed, a mid-single-digit revenue decline deleverages into a low-to-mid single-digit EBITDA decline → yr-2 CF −5.6%, plus the +150 bps rate shock. **No contracted floor exists to cite** — the filings show no multi-year backlog or quantified recurring share (DATA 12), so Bear may fall below any informal "floor"; ad budgets are discretionary, not contracted.

**Pre-mortem (we lost 50% in five years):** A 2027–28 ad recession hits local/regional budgets exactly as political spend normalizes; programmatic stalls at ~10% of digital revenue and the mix-shift margin story dies; AFFO lands below the $8.75 guide, forcing a dividend cut that breaks the income bid; the multiple compresses from ~24x to ~14x owner earnings (the Bear value $87.81 is −39%; a second leg of de-rating plus a rate shock reaches −50%). ## SECTION 9 — RED TEAM

**Strongest short thesis:** At ~$144 the stock pays ~26x trailing GAAP earnings (AAII value grade F, "ultra Expensive") after a +93% three-year run and +16% six-month rise. FY2027 consensus growth is only +3.9% revenue / +7.0% EPS — the midterm political year inflates the base, programmatic (>50% but ~10% of digital revenue) decelerates off its base, the 5.3% 10y caps REIT multiples, and the revision cycle has visibly stalled (two downgrades, zero upgrades). Any FY2027 miss gets both a growth and a multiple haircut.

**My answer:** The reverse DCF under the *neutral* structure shows the market is pricing only +3.65% 10-year CAGR — **below** the median base rate for this size bucket. Nobody is paying for heroics; the price pays ~24x for a business whose own record supports 8–10% near-term owner-earnings growth, a 52.9% return on tangible invested capital, and a record margin that the desk conservatively fades to trend by year 10 (implied terminal multiple 21.3x, *below* today's GAAP P/E). The short thesis needs the 21%-probability demand recession to actually materialize — until then it is a valuation-complaint about a business that keeps raising guidance. But I concede the asymmetry: upside to Bull is +7%, downside to Bear is −39%. That is precisely why value says HOLD and only a trend-disciplined, small momentum position is defensible at this price.
